params.name: id
params.description: Look up a single offering by its exact prefixed ID (e.g. offer_6a4f69ee490f66322f968b87). Use this when you already know the offering ID and want to confirm it exists before updating it.

params.name: name_contains
params.description: Find offerings whose name contains specific text (case-insensitive). For example, pass "summer" to find all summer-related offerings.

params.name: status_in
params.description: Filter by lifecycle status. Valid values: active, scheduled, expired, archived, draft. Example: status_in=active,scheduled

params.name: tags
params.description: Filter to offerings that have ALL of the specified tags. Repeat the parameter for multiple tags: tags=summer-sale&tags=vip-users.

params.name: created_date_gte
params.description: List offerings created on or after this date. Format: YYYY-MM-DD.

params.name: created_date_lte
params.description: List offerings created on or before this date. Format: YYYY-MM-DD.

params.name: created_by
params.description: Filter offerings created by specific team members. Pass one or more email addresses. Example: created_by=john.doe@example.com,marketing-team@example.com

params.name: fields
params.description: Request only the fields you need. Example: fields=id,name,status returns only those three fields per item.

params.name: cursor
params.description: Pagination cursor returned as `next_cursor` in the previous response. Omit on the first request. When `next_cursor` is `null` in the response, you have reached the last page.

items.docs:
Fetch all offerings in the workspace. Returns a summary of each offering — ID, name,
status, tags, and creation metadata.
Create a new Offering in the workspace.

params.name: offer_id
params.description: The unique ID of the offering to be updated. You can fetch the offering ID using the [List Offerings API](/api/public-offerings/list-offerings) by filtering with name.

items.docs:
Modify an existing offering. Only the fields you include in the request body are
changed.

params.name: cursor
params.description:
An opaque pagination token used to retrieve the next page of results.

* **Initial Request:** Omit this parameter entirely on the first call to fetch the beginning of the list.
* **Subsequent Pages:** Pass the exact string received from the `next_cursor` field of the immediate previous response.
* **Handling:** Pass this token completely verbatim. Do not decode, alter, or modify the string in any way.

params.name: limit
params.description: Number of templates per page. Default 20, maximum 100.
